meaning: A printed list of names, addresses and phone numbers, in A to Z order. The phone company brought it to your door.
clues: A printed book that the telephone company delivered to homes. It lists people's names and numbers in A to Z order.
A second part, on yellow paper, listed shops and firms by kind.
The very first one, in 1878, was a single cardboard sheet listing 50 names.
When people began to look up numbers online, some places stopped sending it to each home.
It has two words. The first starts with P, and the second has four letters.

decoys.meaning: A rotating file of index cards on a desk. You flip to a letter to find someone's address or number.
A phone service where an operator looks up a number for you and reads it aloud.
A book listing a town's people with their addresses and jobs. The first ones in America came out in 1785.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Every name sat in plain A to Z order, so anyone could look someone up. Any good list works that way.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Today's version: your phone's contacts. Type a few letters of a name, tap it, and tap Call.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back then, being 'in the book' meant people could find you. A contact list is the same idea.
